lines: Before breakfast, the brass Star Door woke with a clunk.
A note! It says: Find nothing. Five clues will show the way.
Find nothing? Easy. I am brilliant at finding things that are not there!
Then we start with what the door gave us: a real note and five empty star spaces.
The first clue was tucked inside the parcel. Sol reached in.
My toy! I knew I packed you.
Now the box has nothing in it.
Look again, Sol. Move the toy, then look inside the box.
The toy is outside. The empty box is still here. Empty means the toy is not inside.
The brass bell hung still. Nori leaned close to listen.
I heard no ring. But I heard my breath, and the bell stayed right there.
This card has nothing on it. Shall we test that?
Use your finger. Make a mark, or choose to leave the card blank.
A mark is something we can see. A blank card is still a card. Neither choice made nothing appear.
The card made the wall tiles glow.
They want us to spell the mystery word. Step with me.
Nothing is a word we can see, say and read. The word did not vanish when we named it.
I can make Sol's toy vanish. Watch!
There it is. Hidden is not gone. The curtain only changed what we could see.
Five clues. Five stars. The Star Door is opening!
Two little doors waited. Door A offered a card. Door B offered no object.
The note said, find nothing. Which door showed us nothing?
Neither door showed nothing. A showed a card. B showed no object, so we do not invent one.
The crew carried the bright map into the library. Its first star blinked.
Before we file it: what did Sol call empty?
The box was here. The toy was outside. We found no nothing, and we never had to pretend.
